Eight weeks after a tick bite, a 33-year-old male patient presented with stiffness of one leg together with spasmodic painful jerks resembling stiff man syndrome.
One week later he began to suffer from nocturnal pain in the left leg.
Clinically, his disease may be characterized as a partial stiff man syndrome with muscle rigidity and painful myoclonic jerks confined to the left lower leg.

extractions.value: Clinical features (stiffness and spasmodic jerks confined to one leg), CSF findings (elevated cell counts and protein, intrathecal synthesis of Borrelia burgdorferi-specific IgG), positive serology for B. burgdorferi, EMG findings (tonic firing of normal motor units, reflex myoclonus with spinal localization), and exclusion of local tetanus.
extractions.quote: The clinical picture of this patient showed some resemblance to the stiff man syndrome. However, it was confined to one leg and its infectious origin was confirmed by CSF findings, positive serology and the demonstration of intrathecally produced, oligoclonal, B. burgdorferi-specific IgG bands.

extractions.value: The patient had a tick bite in the left lower quadrant of the abdomen 9 weeks before admission. Creatine kinase levels were elevated at 878 units/l, dropping to normal (77 units/l) 1 week after initiation of therapy. The case is presented as Borrelia burgdorferi myelitis presenting as a partial stiff man syndrome.
